content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To go fishing anymore, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Renew the state fishing license online (15 minutes)
Step 2. Research the current migration patterns of local trout (2 hours)
Step 3. Inspect the integrity of the fiberglass rod (10 minutes)
Step 4. Buy a heavy-duty waterproof tackle box (30 minutes)
Step 5. Purchase a specialized trout lure set (20 minutes)
Step 6. Check the local weather forecast for the weekend (5 minutes)
Step 7. Locate the hidden mountain trailhead on a map (1 hour)
Step 8. Gather all old fishing gear from the garage (45 minutes)
Step 9. Organize lures by depth and color (1 hour)
Step 10. Tie a series of high-strength leader knots (30 minutes)
Step 11. Pack a first-aid kit with antiseptic (10 minutes)
Step 12. Apply waterproof sealant to wading boots (24 hours)
Step 13. Double-check the final gear checklist (15 minutes)
Step 14. Clean the reel's internal ball bearings (40 minutes)
Step 15. Buy a new spool of 8lb monofilament line (20 minutes)
Step 16. Load the car with all prepared equipment (20 minutes)
Step 17. Fill the portable cooler with ice packs (5 minutes)
Step 18. Sort through the fly-tying materials (1 hour)
Step 19. Purchase a variety of live bait (30 minutes)
Step 20. Charge the portable GPS unit (4 hours)
Step 21. Pack a lunch with high-protein snacks (20 minutes)
Step 22. Oil the mechanical joints of the folding chair (15 minutes)
Step 23. Place the tackle box in the trunk (5 minutes)
Step 24. Test the tension on the drag system (10 minutes)
Step 25. Clean the polarized sunglasses (5 minutes)
Step 26. Check the battery levels in the headlamp (5 minutes)
Step 27. Sharpen the hooks on all secondary lures (1 hour)
Step 28. Scrub the dried mud off the fishing vest (30 minutes)
Step 29. Apply UV protectant spray to the rod (15 minutes)
Step 30. Find the spare keys to the roof rack (20 minutes)
Step 31. Refill the reusable water canteen (5 minutes)
Step 32. Verify the lake's current water levels (30 minutes)
Step 33. Spool the new line onto the reel (20 minutes)
Step 34. Check for any local fishing bans or restrictions (30 minutes)
Step 35. Attach the leader line to the main line (10 minutes)
Step 36. Test the waterproof seal on the phone case (10 minutes)
Step 37. Set the alarm clock for 4:00 AM (2 minutes)
Step 38. Inspect the net for any holes (15 minutes)
Step 39. Lubricate the hinges on the truck tailgate (10 minutes)
Step 40. Download offline maps for the remote area (15 minutes)
Step 41. Buy a wide-brimmed sun hat (25 minutes)

Step 45. Replace the worn-out felt soles on boots (1 hour)
Step 46. Buy a bottle of insect repellent (10 minutes)

Step 48. Print out a hard copy of the topographic map (5 minutes)
Step 49. Fill a thermos with hot coffee (10 minutes)
Step 50. Test the emergency whistle (2 minutes)
Step 51. Pack a lightweight rain poncho (5 minutes)
Step 52. Attach the fishing license to the vest (5 minutes)
Step 53. Put the multi-tool in the side pocket (2 minutes)
Step 54. Store the live bait in a breathable container (10 minutes)
Step 55. Select the starting lure for the morning (5 minutes)
Step 56. Mend any small tears in the landing net (30 minutes)
Step 57. Sharpen the fillet knife (15 minutes)
Step 58. Check the spare tire pressure (10 minutes)
Step 59. Review the safety protocol for wildlife encounters (30 minutes)
Step 60. Confirm the trip details with a friend (10 minutes)
Step 61. Place the knife and tools in the safety sheath (5 minutes)
Step 62. Finalize the choice of fishing spot (1 hour)
Step 63. Calibrate the handheld barometer (15 minutes)
Step 64. Apply a fresh coat of wax to the rod (30 minutes)
Step 65. Watch a video on new casting techniques (20 minutes)
Step 66. Pack a small portable stove (15 minutes)
Step 67. Buy a heavy-duty dry bag (45 minutes)
Step 68. Verify the sunrise time (5 minutes)
Step 69. Test the floating capability of the net (10 minutes)
Step 70. Clean the debris out of the waders (20 minutes)
Step 71. Replace the rusted split rings on lures (45 minutes)
Step 72. Check the grip on the wading staff (10 minutes)
Step 73. Inspect the trailer hitch (15 minutes)
Step 74. Organize the trunk for maximum space (20 minutes)
Step 75. Pack the polarized sunglasses in their case (2 minutes)
Step 76. Hang the vest by the door (2 minutes)
Step 77. Apply sunblock to face and neck (5 minutes)
Step 78. Set out the clothes for the morning (10 minutes)
Step 79. Check the guides on the rod for cracks (15 minutes)
Step 80. Pre-cut several lengths of tippet material (15 minutes)
